title: Post-Apocalyptic Rally: Helmet Collector
description: A post-apocalyptic driving game where the player steers a concept car through a desolate arena collecting damaged helmets scattered across the ground. The player must navigate the car using keyboard controls, collect at least 6 helmets by driving close to them, and reach a finish zone before a 60-second timer expires.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a post-apocalyptic rally collection game. Load CarConcept.glb as the player vehicle and DamagedHelmet.glb to spawn 8 collectible helmets placed at random positions on a large flat ground plane (100x100 units). Setup: Create a dark ground plane with a GridHelper overlay to suggest cracked terrain. Use a HemisphereLight (orange-ish sky, dark ground) and a DirectionalLight with shadows enabled for a moody atmosphere. Place the car at the origin facing forward. Scale the helmets to roughly 1.5 units and position them at random XZ coordinates within a 40-unit radius, each floating 0.5 units above ground and slowly rotating on Y axis. Place a glowing finish zone (a green semi-transparent cylinder) at coordinates (0, 0, -45). Camera: Implement a third-person chase camera that follows behind and above the car, smoothly interpolating position using lerp each frame. Interactions and validation: 1) W key accelerates the car forward in its facing direction (validate speed stays between 0 and 0.4 units per frame). 2) S key decelerates or reverses (validate speed stays above -0.15). 3) A and D keys rotate the car left and right (validate rotation delta is clamped to 0.03 radians per frame). 4) When the car comes within 3 units of a helmet, collect it: remove the helmet from the scene, increment a counter, and play a brief scale-up animation on the car. 5) Display an HTML overlay HUD showing helmets collected out of 8, current speed as a bar, and a 60-second countdown timer. 6) Validate that the player has collected at least 6 helmets before entering the finish zone. 7) When the car enters the finish zone with enough helmets, show a victory screen with time remaining. 8) If the timer hits zero, show a game-over overlay with a restart button. Ensure all parameter bounds are enforced each frame. Add subtle fog to the scene for atmosphere.
